content: Netupitant/palonosetron capsules are indicated for use in combination with dexamethasone in adults to prevent both acute and delayed nausea and vomiting associated with cancer chemotherapy, including highly emetogenic chemotherapy. Netupitant/palonosetron injection is indicated for use in combination with dexamethasone in adults to prevent acute and delayed nausea and vomiting associated with initial and repeat courses of highly emetogenic chemotherapy. The safety and efficacy of netupitant/palonosetron in patients under 18 years of age have not been established. Use caution when dosing elderly patients, as they are more likely to have reduced hepatic, renal, or cardiac function, as well as concomitant diseases or other drug therapies. Netupitant/palonosetron is contraindicated with apomorphine due to reports of profound hypotension and loss of consciousness when 5-HT3 antagonists are coadministered with apomorphine. Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated due to the risk of severe hypotension or syncope. Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated as lonafarnib is a sensitive CYP3A4 substrate. Netupitant/palonosetron and almotriptan may increase each other's toxicity through serotonin level interactions. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Netupitant is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4. Avoid use in patients who are chronically using strong CYP3A4 inducers, such as carbamazepine. If short-term use of moderate CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the cobimetinib dose to 20 mg. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor.
